text:
ben_sales: Quick update — Horizon finished their POC throughput sweep on our dedicated cluster this morning. They asked for a consolidated results summary and a quote that factors in sustained QPS + burst capacity. Can ops/bench help verify numbers?

alexa_k: Sending artifacts now. s3://redwood-poc/horizon/2026-03-20/bench-results.tar.gz :thumbsup:

maya_r: I pulled the logs. Main run: 1.5k sustained QPS, 10k peak bursts for ~30s. Avg token latency ~120ms, 95th ~220ms for 512-token traffic. Tail gets noisy during bursts.

samir_m: Can you paste the wrk command used so I can reproduce?

ben_sales: They used our reference harness, roughly:

```
wrk -t12 -c800 -d600s --latency 
  --script=redwood_chat.lua 
  --timeout 30s 
  --rate 1500
```

alexa_k: Also ran a variant with adaptive routing to cheaper model during overload. Metrics attached in artifacts: throughput.csv, latency_pcts.json, model_switch_events.log

maya_r: Quick note: the adaptive routing cut cost by ~18% but increased 95th latency by ~30ms during switch windows. See model_switch_events.log for timings.

liz_p: For quoting: Horizon needs SLA for 95th <250ms sustained and ability to handle 10k microbursts (30s). They asked whether dedicated pool + burst buffer is recommended and what monthly commit looks like.

samir_m: From infra side — to reliably hit 1.5k sustained with 95th <250ms we need reserved 6x A100-equivalent GPUs in dedicated, with autoscale headroom to add 2 GPUs for burst smoothing. If they want 10k bursts we need burst pool or cross-region fallback.

ben_sales: Can you give a quick cost delta between: (A) dedicated reserved + burst pool, (B) hosted with adaptive routing + per-token bill? Need numbers to feed to sales deck.

samir_m: Rough back-of-envelope:
- Option A (reserved): ~$45k/mo for reserved capacity (6 GPUs) + burst buffer ops ~$8k/mo amortized for occasional add.
- Option B (hosted adaptive): $0 base commit, estimated token bill ~$60k/mo at their traffic profile, with ~20% variance.

maya_r: Also attach perf notes: warm KV cache was crucial. Cold starts spiked p95 to ~900ms for first 10k requests. Recommend warmup sequence before SLA windows.

alexa_k: Repro steps I ran in k8s if you want to replicate locally:

```
helm upgrade --install redwood-poc ./charts/poc --set replicaCount=6 --set concurrency=256
kubectl apply -f poc-ramp.yaml
```

ben_sales: Horizon asked about security questionnaire implications for Dedicated vs Hosted. Can security team confirm whether audit logs + KMS are available on Dedicated?

liz_p: Yes — Dedicated includes KMS integration, syslog/ audit export, and optional HSM. We'll include that in the answer doc.

samir_m: One more perf caveat: when adaptive routing triggers model switch, we see a short (2-5s) throughput dip while KV cache repopulates. For microbursts that matters. Suggest configuring fallback policy to route to same architecture quantized variant where possible.

maya_r: TL;DR for sales deck:
- Sustained 1.5k QPS achievable with 6 reserved GPUs + cache warmup
- 10k bursts require burst pool or cross-region fallback; expect ~2-5s dip during model switch without prewarmed cache
- Cost: reserved ~45k/mo + burst buffer ~8k/mo vs hosted token bill ~60k/mo (subject to traffic variance)
- Security: Dedicated supports KMS/HSM + audit export

ben_sales: This is perfect — can someone turn the TL;DR into a 1-paragraph summary + a short pricing table for the deck? Also include recommended warmup command and the WRK line.

alexa_k: I'll draft the paragraph and attach a small CSV with the cost numbers. Will ping when ready.

deploy-bot: Artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-poc/horizon/2026-03-20/bench-results.tar.gz (6 files)

ben_sales: Thanks all. If we can get the summary + quote by EOD I'll share with Horizon. :pray:
